pcs.pc_description: Obtain the receiving and unloading schedule, including docking bay and time of transport arrival from the supervisor.
Arrange necessary material handling equipment, tools, tackles, chains, and ropes for unloading.
Ensure that the unloading area is clear of obstacles and Wear the appropriate PPE required for operations.
Visually inspect the goods to be unloaded for any damage, leakage or discrepancies.
Cross-check the goods against the purchase order/ unloading schedule and ensure that the quantity, type of products, item codes, etc., match.
Report to the supervisor in case of discrepancies and document the information accordingly.
Use the appropriate tools, ropes/chains to secure the product/crate and operate MHE to load or unload the items from the pallet/ racks/ vehicle as required.
Deliver the unloaded packages to the specified location as per the instructions.
Report any breakages or spillages of package or consignment during unloading.
Obtain shipping order/ dispatch list/ loading schedule for the day from the Supervisor.
Ensure that all goods are in good condition for shipment and that they are properly packaged and labelled for transportation.
Collect necessary tools/ equipment, PPE, and MHE based on the products handled and scheduled.
Secure the loads using proper tools to the MHE and move goods to the loading bay.
Check the vehicle and driver details before loading the goods into the vehicle.
Load the goods inside the vehicle and check for any damage.
In case of any damage, Move damaged goods to the quarantine area and report to the supervisor.
Park the MHE at the designated parking location and submit a daily report to the supervisor.

pcs.pc_description: Receive goods movement checklist from supervisor/executive and check product packaging for damages and defects at the time of receipt.
Inform supervisor/executive of the damages and segregate damaged goods/packages.
Carry packages to the internal warehouse using forklift or other material handling equipment.
Segregate and move goods to the appropriate sub stores depending upon the storage requirements such as cold storage or ambient storage.
Unpack crates/packages and sort goods as per product type and specification.
Load materials to designated storage areas such as racks, shelves etc. as per quantity specification, using Material Handling Equipment (MHE) such as dollies, forklifts, hand trucks etc.
Check raw materials/items for damages and spillages and segregate the same.
Discard packaging materials such as foam, bubble wrap, cardboard as per Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
Record quantity/ weight/ volume of goods received, moved and stored.
Inform supervisors on the quantity of damaged items and move them to containment area of the warehouse.
Submit daily reports to the supervisor.
Receive inventory sheet data from the supervisor and identify the right component/product to be counted.
Perform inventory checks as per SOP using barcode/ label scanners, manual counting, weight/ volume inspection, or other stock counting techniques.
Count items manually, if required, and mark them off on inventory sheets.
Check that the physical stock matches the digital or written records.
Verify inventory/product labels and report errors/ damages.
Carry out spot checks of sections to ensure that inventory was counted correctly.
Cross-check the inventory count to see if the audit produces an error.
Report any damage or spillages and the status of inventory to the supervisor.
Support effective pest control activities as per the requirements to protect the quality of materials stored.
Clean and maintain the warehouse using brooms, rags and other appropriate cleaning gear.
Store warehouse MHE in the appropriate location and perform daily maintenance checks as per SOP.

pcs.pc_description: Obtain kitting list from supervisor and details of shift schedule for kitting.
Use the appropriate PPE based on the product and environment.
Collect the appropriate number of bins/ crates/ fixtures to be used for kitting.
Check items received for kitting for damages, bar code /product label errors and report the same to supervisor.
Segregate items to be kitted and check Bill of Material (BOM) for any missing components and report the same to supervisor.
Receive replacement or missing components.
Kit the items in the assigned bin/crate/fixture as per the BOM.
Ensure the right quantity and quality of items are placed on the bin/crate/fixture.
Clean the area after kitting operation and submit daily reports to supervisor reporting total kitting done, damages, delays and accidents.

Transport the loaded goods to the line feeding location at the right time as per specified instructions.
Exercise caution while operating the MHE and follow speed, turning, horn usage, right of way, parking and other instructions as per SOP.
Match the part numbers on the label with the feeding location label as per SOP.
Store/feed the components/parts to the line to process as per SOP.

Deliver the empty bins/crates/ fixtures at the assigned area of the store/warehouse.
Collect goods rejected at the line from the line store and transport it back to the assigned location in the warehouse/ store.
Collect excess/un-used goods from the line store and transport it back to the assigned location in the warehouse/store.
Submit periodic and end of day reports on picking, line feeding, line rejections etc. to supervisor.
Park the MHE at the appropriate location and recharge its batteries if required.

pcs.pc_description: Obtain the picklist/ order forms from the supervisor for picking and arrange for Machine Handling Equipment (MHE), equipment, tools and PPE required.
Arrange for various equipment such as bins/ fixtures/ crates and stationery to facilitate picking activity.
Confirm the order details and prioritise them based on factors such as urgency (next-day or same-day shipments), Specific customer or department needs, Shipping schedule or location, etc.
Select the appropriate picking method according to location, type of available picking method, equipment, product, etc.
Identify the location of items listed in the pick list manually or by using technology.
Account for any specific handling requirements (fragile, perishable, custom orders).
Operate MHE or use the MHE operator to pick the items from the pallets/ bins/ cartons/racks/ yard as required.
Ensure that the correct number of units are picked up and that there is no visible damage.
Place the items in the bin/fixture/crate as per the holding capacity and the quantity requisitioned.
Confirm that all items in the order are correct (i.e., the correct SKU, size, and quantity).
Deliver items for kiting/line feeding/ packing area as per the instructions.

Prepare the packing area and gather all necessary packing materials as per the packing slip, such as boxes (a variety of sizes), Bubble wrap, foam inserts, packing peanuts, or air cushions for protection, Tape (packing tape or strong adhesive tape), Scissors or tape dispensers, invoice, and any other documentation
Identify any fragile or temperature-sensitive items that require special handling during packing.
Check that the correct items and quantities match the order, including SKU numbers, product codes, and descriptions.
Choose appropriate packing materials as per the items being packed and transportation.
Ensure that all items are arranged properly inside the box with proper layering and cushioning to avoid damage during shipping.
Make sure all seams and edges are sealed to prevent the box from opening during transit.

Prepare the Shipping Label by updating all the necessary information, such as the Recipient's Information (Name, address, and contact details of the recipient/ customer or internal department), the Sender's Information, the order/Tracking Number, the Shipping Method and the shipping service, the Package Weight and Dimensions, and the Handling Instructions.
Generate, Print and attach the label to the package securely.
Conduct a final visual check and move the packages to the shipping area.

modules.module_title: Handle leather in the plant warehouse

pcs.pc_description: Inspect the quality of the leather and check for damage while receiving it inside the warehouse.
Store leather away from light and at room temperature (65° to 72°F) with around 55% humidity to avoid mold and mildew growth.
Segregate leather as per grades A, B and C and store the same kind of leather together.
Handle leather with a clean hand or wear gloves and avoid dragging or dropping leather rolls or hides.
Ensure that leather is kept off the floor and place it on shelves high enough to prevent the moisture from creeping into the leather.
Check the leather for damages and defects, wrap the leather in paper, and ensure the leather is not folded.
Avoid creases or deformation, and avoid metal contact with leather, as this reacts with the leather and destroys its commercial value.
Keep coloured leather separate from others, as it may lead to dye transfer.
Place oily leather away from non-oily leather by keeping an impenetrable barrier between them.
Ensure that powder and oil do not spill over the leather.
Ensure that leather is stored in a controlled environment, such as temperature (around 65-75°F) and humidity (around 50-60%), and there is no direct sunlight.
Check for the presence of rodents, birds, insects and other pests which affect the cargo and undertake pest control activity at the warehouse as per SOP.
Ensure that the leather is not stacked very high, as too much pressure on the leather leads to wrinkles and damage.
Inspect the leather stored in the warehouse regularly to avoid damage.

pcs.pc_description: Visually inspect raw materials while receiving them for any signs of damage or Quality Issues.
Identify and comply with coding requirements for storage of FMCG goods.
Segregate raw materials as per the storage requirements into ambient or cold storage in a manner that allows for easy identification and retrieval.
Ensure that temperature-sensitive FMCG items, like frozen food, dairy, or beverages, are stored in appropriate refrigerated or freezer units and that temperature logs are regularly checked.
Check to ensure that products are not stored adjacent to waste or non-product items.
Dispose of packaging material as per standard operating procedure.
Make arrangements for equipment/tools such as pallets, reach stack, forklift, PPE, etc., according to the kind of product to be handled.
Take the assistance of the MHE operator to pick the items from the pallet or racks, if required.
Execute different types of picking such as single order picking, batch picking, zone picking, pick and pass, multi-batch picking, order consolidation, wave picking, etc.
Sort and place materials or items on racks, shelves, or in bins according to predetermined sequence such as size, type, style, colour, or product code.
Report defective or broken products to the supervisor.
Ensure First-In, First-Out (FIFO)/Last-In, First- Out (LIFO) inventory management as per company/product Standard Operating Procedures (SOP).
Track expiry dates and ensure that any goods approaching expiration are moved to the front for quicker dispatch.
Maintain high personal hygiene and wear protective hair coverage and PPE.

Ensure that the warehouse is regularly cleaned and sanitised, particularly in areas where perishable goods are stored or processed and follow Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for food-related items.
Carry out material handling without product contamination by avoiding eating/drinking and avoiding wearing any jewellery.
Deploy effective pest control services as per pest management standards for food processing and handling facilities.
Comply with regulations prescribed by FSSA, HACCP, ISO 22000:2005, FSMS, AIB, BRC and OSHA.
Check pallets to ensure they are clean, dry, free from mold, odour-free, off infestation, etc., as per norms.

pcs.pc_description: Load goods on fixtures/ crates/ pallets/ boxes
Sort and place materials for items on racks, shelves, or bins according to the Kanban list
Check for adherence to different certifications for automotive goods

pcs.pc_description: Visually inspect the components while receiving them for any visible damage, such as crushed packages, broken parts, or damaged anti- static bags and inspect the parts for scratches or cracks, particularly on microchips or circuit boards
Check to ensure that the temperature of the warehouse is maintained between 15°C to 27°C & 30% to 60% relative humidity
Check for adherence to different certifications for electronic components such as ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, etc
Transport components as per the pick list to the kitting area using MHE if required
Unpack and segregate components carefully, such as the PCB, camera, chips, etc., as per the pick list
Dispose of packaging materials such as plastic films, component tubes, anti-static bags, sheet metal, cast metals, etc., as per standard operating procedure
Handle PCB as per the handling and storage guidelines prescribed in PCB – 1601, ANSI/ESD S20.20 or equivalent
Arrange components in the designated tray based on component size and requirement as per SOP and transport them to the appropriate line feeding area in tote trolleys
Sort components based on usage frequency, i.e., high-demand components should be stored in easily accessible locations, while less frequently used parts can be placed on more distant or lower shelves
Ensure that all components are labelled with part numbers, batch numbers, and descriptions
Organise components into categories such as resistors, capacitors, microchips, connectors, transistors, circuit boards, etc. Each category may have different storage requirements

Store heavier or larger components (such as power supplies) on lower shelves to prevent accidents, while smaller components (such as SMDs or resistors) should be stored in bins, drawers, or trays for easy access
Store components according to the storage instructions and specific needs, such as Antistatic Storage for ICs (integrated circuits) or capacitors
Perform regular cycle counts to ensure that the physical inventory matches the system’s records

Use tweezers, vacuum pick-up tools, or automated pickers for small or delicate components to avoid damaging parts during retrieval
Ensure clean work areas and use cleanroom environments if necessary for sensitive parts to keep components free from contaminants such as dust, grease, or fingerprints

Report defective or broken components to the supervisor, document any damage or quality issues with components upon receipt or during storage and follow the appropriate procedures for returning or replacing parts
Perform pest control to avoid destruction from pests such as insects, mice, and rats
Submit a daily report to the supervisor

Segregate material as per batch/lot wise and transfer the cleaned containers/packs onto the clean pallet
Transfer the cleaned container/pack top to the weighing area by using the appropriate MHE
Check the cleanliness of the balance and ensure its routine calibration as per SOP
Weigh the containers/ packs received one by one on the balance provided and ensure that the quantity received is equal to that mentioned in the delivery documents

modules.module_title: Storage of raw materials in the plant

pcs.pc_description: Store materials in climate-controlled environments to prevent degradation due to high or low temperatures and humidity

Separate materials based on their risk category or type, such as Chemicals and Solvents (flammable/ corrosive/ hazardous), Biological Materials (bacterial cultures or vaccines), Raw Powders and Crystals, and Controlled Substances (e.g., narcotics, controlled drugs)

• Segregate raw materials as per the required storage conditions as stated on the label, such as: • • store in ‘cold’ temperature. • • store in temperature between 2°C to 8°C. • • store below 15°C temperature. • • store in “Deep Freezer”. • • store in a “Cool” place. • • store below 25°C.
Organise materials by lot number or batch number for traceability, ensuring the traceback process in case of product recalls or quality control issues
Use the FIFO system to ensure older materials are used before newer ones, preventing expiration or degradation
Conduct regular cycle counts and periodic inventory audits and document them
If QC rejects the material, transport it back to the rejected storage area and inform the Supervisor
Check the temperature of the storage area, and in case it exceeds the limit, inform the maintenance department
Ensure that clean, appropriate equipment (e.g., scoops, weighing scales, or dispensing containers) is used for handling and dispensing
Make sure that raw materials used for different products are handled separately to prevent cross-contamination

Ensure that all materials are appropriately labelled as per Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and regulatory standards (e.g., FDA, EMA) and with information such as batch number, content status, expiry date, etc
Handle nearby expiry products as per SOP and manufacturer's guidelines
Follow Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), FDA regulations, and other relevant standards to ensure raw materials are stored, handled, and disposed of in compliance with industry standards
Ensure proper MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheets) are available and that safety protocols, such as proper ventilation or spill containment procedures, are followed
Dispose of waste and expired materials in compliance with environmental regulations and hazardous waste disposal guidelines

pcs.pc_description: Feed and append inventory data received from respective departments into the ERP system.
Make a list of all the inventory with clear details, including item code, item name, unit name, product description, purchase price, sales price, tax code, tracking code, etc.
Prepare MIS report containing Current stock levels, Safety Stock, Inventory Turnover, etc.
Recheck the inventory data to identify any unusual information and take corrective action.
Update inventory items as and when there are changes and Ensure discrepancies between physical and system records are identified and resolved.
Ensure that the inventory is classified as per the type, function and requirements, e.g. Raw Materials, Work-in-Progress (WIP), Finished Goods, Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) Supplies, etc.
Review the current stock levels of each category and check the reorder point (ROP) for each inventory item based on historical demand and lead times.
Using various inventory analysis methods, such as ABC, VED, and FSN analysis, determine the optimum amount of inventory (Economic Order Quantity (EOQ)) to be kept on hand.
Review the inventory on a continuous or periodic basis as pre-decided by the manager.
Submit the analysis to the manager for further review.
Review historical usage, recent stockouts and demand patterns for materials and components.
Determine the period of forecasting based on the manufacturing production cycle, inventory turnover rate, etc., and collect all past demand data.

Choose the right forecasting method, such as qualitative forecasting (Delphi method, historical life cycle analogy) or quantitative forecasting (time series models, exponential smoothing, seasonal indexes), according to business needs and suitability.
Use forecasting models (e.g., moving averages, exponential smoothing) to predict future demand.
Consider factors like production schedules, seasonal variations, and potential supply chain disruptions.
Evaluate both long-term and short-term influencers and outside variables for forecasting.

Perform inventory forecasting techniques as per standard operating procedures, considering both long-term, short-term, and outside variables such as economic growth, seasonality, lifestyle changes, etc.
Compare actual demand against forecasts from multiple angles to identify the variances.
Diagnose the cause of forecast variances, such as inaccurate inventory data, poor forecasting, variability in demand, swings in the economy, etc. and take corrective actions.
